rationale: The published literature on biallelic GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder with dysmorphic facies, brain anomalies, and seizures (NEDFBS; OMIM #621201) documents a cumulative total of 17 affected individuals as of 2026. Abdel et al. (2025) reported 4 patients from 3 unrelated families, while López et al. (2026) described a novel affected individual alongside a systematic aggregation of all 16 previously reported cases across the literature (including De Hayr et al., 2025 and earlier cohort reports), bringing the worldwide definitive cohort to exactly 17 patients.

evidence.text: López et al. (2026) reported an affected individual with novel biallelic variants in GTF3C3 and conducted a comprehensive review and comparative genotypic/phenotypic analysis of all 16 previously reported individuals in the literature, compiling the total definitive cohort of 17 patients.

evidence.text: Abdel et al. (2025) established the association between biallelic GTF3C3 variants and NEDFBS by reporting 4 individuals from 3 unrelated families presenting with developmental delay, intellectual disability, microcephaly, characteristic facial dysmorphisms, cerebellar/brain atrophy, and seizures (2/4 patients).

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Herein, we describe the identification of biallelic variants in GTF3C3, which encodes a key component of the TFIIIC subunit, in four patients from three unrelated families of different ethnicities collected through GeneMatcher.

evidence.text: ClinVar variation record for GTF3C3 cites OMIM #621201 and independently references clinical descriptions of biallelic GTF3C3 cases including De Hayr et al. (2025).

new_directions.question_text: What are the standardized Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) frequencies across all 17 individuals summarized by López et al. (2026)?
new_directions.rationale: Extracting granular numerators and denominators for recurrent dysmorphic features (e.g., prominent nasal bridge, microcephaly) and neuroimaging hallmarks (cerebellar atrophy, simplified gyral pattern) is essential for differential diagnostic scoring tools.

new_directions.question_text: Does residual TFIIIC2 complex activity correlate with epilepsy penetrance and severity of brain malformations between truncating/nonsense variants and missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: Abdel et al. identified both missense (p.Cys172Gly, p.Val427Phe, p.Ala509Thr) and nonsense (p.Arg717Ter) variants; understanding whether null alleles present with early intractable seizures versus milder presentation in missense variants will refine genotype-phenotype correlations.
